summary: Tanero Sasakawa (1870–1949) worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tang Yijie (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He served as a professor at Peking University (~1980–2014) and held a post at Stanford University (~1990–1991).

Tania Singer studied at the University of Marburg (~1989–1992), Technical University of Berlin (~1992–1996), and Free University of Berlin (~1996–2000). She held posts at the University of Zurich (~2006–2010) and University of Leipzig (~2010–2019).

Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and Xianlin Ji, and earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. He held a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and he founded the Kangien academy in 1801.

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yushima Seido, Shoheizaka Gakumonjo, and under Genken Taki, Eizen Jitsuyama, and Honko Fugai. He held posts at the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), University of Tokyo (1879), and Komazawa University (1891).

Tao Jiang works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo, among other teachers, and served as an Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander Leonhard Mayer.
Tao Pan works in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle works in Buddhist and religious studies. She served at Emory University as a lecturer and director of its Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Tarab Tulku XI (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1966–1998) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1970–2000).

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Tarthang Monastery and under several traditional teachers. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), Padma Ling (~1969), Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Rabgey specializes in Tibetology and studied at Magdalen College, Harvard University, the University of Cambridge, and University College, Toronto. She held posts at the University of Virginia (~2008–2011) and Georgetown University.

Tashi Samphel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Central School for Tibetans, Dalhousie, and under numerous teachers, he served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1992), Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014–2019).

Tatiana Oranskaia works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1967–1972) and the Central Institute of Hindi (1988), and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Komazawa University in 1978. He held teaching posts at Komazawa University (~1964–1995), Tokai University, and Ryukoku University (attested 1974).

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1918–1921). He held posts at Hosei University (~1925–1932), Meiji University (~1946–1964), Toyo University, Tsuda University, and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied and earned a doctorate at Kyoto University (1948–1962). He held multiple professorial and administrative posts at Kyoto University (1956–1992) and at NACSIS (1992–1994).

Tatsushi Tamai specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a Visiting Researcher at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (attested 2010–2016).
